details.effects: Only thin stems separate; only reed has a strand law (existing reed law: 1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, 8 MPa x (1 - 0.55 x water share 0.9), creep 0.003); dry grass reports the gap. A sample is split, bent, twisted and pulled at 5 N, kept as a tested lot or cracked scrap, and reports only separation, retained twist, fractures and force. Make round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and derives the cord from conserved volume: two plies, each half the solid volume over length x 1.155 twist take-up + 0.02 m loose ends; plies of 1-12 mm and strands no shorter than a ply, else a measured shortfall returns the fiber. The release check needs condition 0.5 and gives an owned untested cord. Trial force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, grip 10000 N/m x cord width); breaking force = 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition. It records grip slip, extension and creep; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands; a break leaves two owned fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. A pass means only that force for that time. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.

details.effects: crossing-contact@1 keeps all three items; the binding is a relation. Round 1 measures each piece by the existing branch law (2 m, 350 kg/m3 solid, water share 0.5, section from volume) and the cord: width w, cord-knot@1 bend limit R. The wrap runs in the obtuse bisector plane round both sections (ellipses r and r/sin b, offset w/2): two half perimeters + sides, routed 0.04 m loose. Closure: each end turns half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), pi Rc + w each (formed at 0.02 m opening); tails need 0.02 m + w, ends a 0.02 m pinch. A short cord, a crossing over 0.1 m thick for one hand or over 100 N x health/100 to lift: paid measured shortfall. Hand-held stages relax when interrupted. Release check: the cord-bend@1 tail rule (reed friction 0.3) must hold 5 N; then 5 N wrap tension. Trial: one hand per piece beyond the crossing; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x piece width); separate: tension max(5 N, F/2) against closure slip and cord break (fiber-cord force / (1 + w/2R)); slide: slips at 0.3 (reed on bark) x tension x top contact angle. Records bending, creep slack, damage over half breaking load, fragments. Carrying hangs the bottom piece. Untie needs condition 0.5. Bound cords wear 0.0005 per round. No reward or shelter.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none.
